lessons.title: Iker Casillas: A captain’s honours
lessons.subtitle: Club success and Spain’s golden era

story.title: A long Madrid chapter
story.body: Casillas’s Real Madrid career brought him 19 titles as a madridista. Three were Champions League trophies, part of an honours collection built over many seasons. Those honours add a new layer to his 725 official appearances: the goalkeeper was central to teams that repeatedly reached the top of Europe.

story.title: A champion with Spain
story.body: His international story reached its high point with Spain’s 2010 World Cup win. He also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and again in 2012. Keep the two chapters distinct: Madrid’s 19 titles belong to his club career, while the World Cup and two Euros came with Spain.

lessons.title: Sergio Ramos: A defender’s trophy haul
lessons.subtitle: Four European Cups among 22 titles

story.title: A decorated Madrid career
story.body: Across 16 seasons with Real Madrid, Sergio Ramos collected 22 titles. The defender’s haul included four European Cups, a remarkable return for a player whose decisive moments became part of the club’s biggest nights. His record extends well beyond the 2014 equalizer already connected to La Décima.

story.title: Different competitions, one legacy
story.body: Ramos’s honours also included five LaLiga titles. He captained Madrid through European success and lifted the trophies as the team moved into a new era. Remember the scale of the collection by keeping its parts separate: 22 titles overall, four European Cups, and five Spanish league championships.

lessons.title: Xolos: The road to the top flight
lessons.subtitle: Early milestones on the climb

story.title: A professional beginning
story.body: Club Tijuana’s professional story began with a match on January 14, 2007. Its first title followed in the Apertura 2010 Liga de Ascenso, the second-tier competition. Winning that tournament was a milestone in its own right, but it did not yet mean promotion: Xolos still had to win a separate two-leg promotion final.

story.title: The climb becomes real
story.body: After the promotion final against Irapuato, Xolos reached Mexico’s top flight in 2011. The club’s Primera División history began on July 23, 2011, against Morelia, with Joe Corona scoring its first goal in that division. Keep the first professional match, the second-tier title, and the top-flight debut as three different milestones.

lessons.title: Madrid’s modern European run
lessons.subtitle: From a three-peat to the 15th crown

story.title: Three in a row
story.body: Madrid’s 2018 victory in Kyiv completed a third consecutive Champions League triumph and brought its European Cup total to 13. That three-peat closed a remarkable five-season stretch in which the club won the competition four times. It connects the earlier European story to a modern period of sustained success.

story.title: The count keeps climbing
story.body: The European Cup count reached 14 when Madrid beat Liverpool in the 2022 final in Paris. Two years later, a win over Borussia Dortmund at Wembley brought the club to 15. Follow the sequence by attaching each number to its year: 13 in 2018, 14 in 2022, and 15 in 2024.
